It is also not appropriate for a Muhaajir to return to the place he migrated from except with good reason." "What is your good reason?" questioned Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA). Hadhrat Waa'il (RA) replied, "The statement of Rasulullaah ﷺ concerning the tribulations. Because of your disputes, I have kept away from you but as soon as you unite, I shall come to you. This is the good reason."
Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) then offered, "I intend making you the governor of Kufa, so proceed there." "I cannot assume a post of governorship from anyone after Rasulullaah ﷺ," Hadhrat Waa'il (RA) replied, "Did you not see that when Abu Bakr (RA) wanted to appoint me as governor, I refused? Thereafter, when Umar (RA) wanted to appoint me as governor, I refused as well and even when Uthmaan (RA) wanted to appoint me as governor, I refused yet again. Despite all of this, I never forsook the pledge of allegiance I took to any of them. The letter of Abu Bakr (RA) came to me when the people from my region had forsaken Islaam and I stood up (to fight in Jihaad) amongst them until Allaah returned them all to the fold of Islaam. This I did without having to fill the post of governorship."
Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) then sent for Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Ummul Hakam (RA) and said to him, "I have made you the governor of Kufa. Go there with Waa'il bin Hujar, honour him and fulfil his needs." Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Your opinion of me is not a good one. You have commanded me to honour someone whom I have seen being honoured by Rasulullaah ﷺ, Abu Bakr (RA), Umar (RA) and Uthmaan (RA) and yourself." This statement made Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) very happy. Hadhrat Waa'il (RA) then proceeded to Kufa with Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) and it was not long thereafter that he passed away.[^1]
The Statement of Hadhrat Abu Barzah Aslami (RA) about the Fight Between Marwaan and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA)

Hadhrat Abul Minhaal reports, "When Ibn Ziyaad was expelled (from Basrah when Yazeed passed away), Marwaan seized power in Shaam, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) seized power in Makkah and a group calling themselves the 'Qurraa' took control of Basrah. My father was extremely grieved about the situation and said (to me), 'May you have no father! Let us go to the companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ Abu Barzah Aslami (RA).' I then accompanied him and when we entered the house, we found Abu Barzah (RA) sitting in the shade of his balcony that was constructed from bamboo.
